title: Design System: QHSEMS Consultancy, Solutions & Training LLP

on-crimson-mut.purpose: The only muted text colour on the crimson CTA band; crimson-tinted, never neutral.

print-ink.purpose: Print stylesheet only; paper gets black type.

display.purpose: Page h1 only; capped at 19-20ch with text-wrap: balance.

lede.purpose: The muted sentence under a heading, 64ch.

label.purpose: Uppercase Archivo eyebrow over a hairline; rule-labels, footer heads, credentials.

code.purpose: Overpass Mono for programme codes, domain numbers and counts only.

subtitle.purpose: h4 at 1.0625rem Archivo 700 - card titles in tracks and footer columns.

block-subhead.purpose: h3 inside a component at 1.125rem - stage-rail items, principle headings, slide-over head.

ui.purpose: The 0.9375rem workhorse - nav, buttons, card prose, catalogue rows, checklists. Dense content drops to this step, never to a private one.

ui-small.purpose: 0.875rem compact controls - btn--sm, filter chips, footer baseline, validation messages.

micro.purpose: 0.8125rem floor - breadcrumbs, field hints, credential pills, footer legal line.

control.purpose: 1rem for every input, select and textarea, so mobile browsers do not zoom on focus.

numeral.purpose: Record-band figures (30+/110K+/80M+); the scale claims are typography.

numeral-small.purpose: 2.25rem per-track programme counts, a half-scale echo of the record band.

glyph.purpose: 1.25rem for every x affordance - search clear, enquiry remove, panel close.

headline-sub.purpose: One step for any h2 heading a sub-section: domain heads, lead-service head, catalogue group heads.

quote.purpose: Pull quote behind a 1px left rule; goals and positioning lines.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Primary button on hover, with translateY(-1px).

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Mobile nav drawer over page content.

shadows.name: slide-over
shadows.purpose: Enquiry panel entering from the right edge.

shadows.name: inset-selection
shadows.purpose: Picked catalogue row; selection drawn inside so footprint never changes.

shadows.name: scrim-nav
shadows.purpose: Scrim behind the open mobile nav.

motion.name: ease-house
motion.purpose: The only easing in the system; all state transitions and panel entries.

motion.name: surface
motion.purpose: Catalogue row and add-button state changes.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: The single authored scroll reveal: opacity 0 + translateY(22px) + blur(6px), IntersectionObserver-driven, gated behind .js, neutralised under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview:
This is a printed technical document taught to behave like a website. Everything is set on white paper, divided by hairlines rather than boxes, and interrupted at intervals by a solid navy band — the way a standards manual alternates body pages with section dividers. Nothing floats. Content blocks have a stroke and a ground; they do not have a shadow, because a capability list is not a physical object you could pick up. Depth exists only where something genuinely moves.

Density is the argument. The catalogue shows 108 named programmes and 75 named consultancy capabilities in full, in scannable rows with monospaced codes, instead of summarising them into three icon cards. That refusal is the system's centre of gravity: where a category site abstracts, this one enumerates, and the layout is tuned to make long enumerations legible — two- and three-column row grids, hairline separators, right-aligned counts, and a sticky filter bar so the list stays navigable at length.

The palette is not chosen, it is sampled: every hue is pulled from the client's logo lockup, and the four pillars (Health green, Safety blue, Environment orange, Training purple) do real work as a coding system rather than decoration. Crimson is the only action colour, and it is rationed. There is no photography anywhere on the site; the hero's process-plant elevation is authored inline SVG line art, and the illustrative register is strictly line, never fill.
keyCharacteristics: Logo-sampled palette; navy ground bands, crimson action, four pillar hues as coding
Archivo 800 display against Source Sans 3 body, Overpass Mono for codes and counts
Hairlines and rules instead of card shadows on content
Enumeration over summary: full lists, monospaced codes, visible counts
Authored line-art SVG only; no photography
One authored motion moment (staggered reveal), reduced-motion honoured

rules.name: The Sampled-Palette Rule
rules.body: Every hue traces to the logo lockup. A new colour is not invented; it is either an existing token or a legibility-corrected variant of one, and the correction is named as such (environ-ink for Environment orange as text).

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: Crimson is the site's only action colour. If an element is crimson it can be clicked, is currently selected, or has failed validation. Pillar colours never become buttons; crimson never becomes a category.

rules.name: The Local Accent Rule
rules.body: Pillar colour is set on the block via --c and read downstream as var(--c, var(--safety)). Never hard-code a pillar hue inside a component — it removes the block's ability to be recoloured.

rules.name: The On-Navy Lift Rule
rules.body: Saturated hues do not survive the navy ground unlifted. On dark bands the record numerals and pillar dots switch to their lifted tints (#FF8FAE, #8FC0F5, #A5DE72, #6FD07F, #7FB6F0, #FFB25E, #C9A0F0), and the hero's emphasis word uses amber #FFC77A. Light passage and dark passage each get their own version of the same colour.

rules.name: The Evidence Mono Rule
rules.body: Overpass Mono is reserved for machine-ish facts — a programme code, a domain number, a count. It never sets a sentence, a label, or a heading.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Archivo headings run 700–800 with negative tracking (-0.028em, tightening to -0.04em on numerals) and line-height at or below 1.2. Display type is compressed; body type is not. Do not set a heading in Source Sans 3.

rules.name: The Count-Is-Visible Rule
rules.body: Wherever a list is grouped, filtered or truncated, its length is stated in type next to its name ("Seven domains · 75 capabilities", "All 108"). The number is the product claim.

rules.name: The Band Rule
rules.body: Vertical structure comes from alternating full-bleed grounds — paper, surface tint, navy — not from boxing content. A new section changes its ground and its padding; it does not get a bordered container around the whole thing.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px line in the line token (or rule-ink on navy). Rows, domains, contact blocks, footer bottom and section heads all divide this way. Heavier strokes are reserved and meaningful: 2px for a coded group head, 3px for a pillar-coded block edge, 1.5px for an interactive edge.

rules.name: The Moving-Surface Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the surface can move or sits above the page. Buttons, the nav drawer and the slide-over panel get one. A card, a list row, a domain block or a band does not — those use a 1px stroke and a ground change instead.

rules.name: The Inset-Selection Rule
rules.body: Selected state is drawn inside the box, not under it: a picked programme row uses box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--c, var(--safety)) with a transparent border, so selection never changes the row's footprint or the list's rhythm.

dos: Do separate with hairlines — 1px line on paper, rule-ink on navy — and reserve 2px/3px strokes for coded group heads and pillar-coded block edges.
Do set pillar colour on the block as an inline --c and read it as var(--c, var(--safety)) inside components.
Do switch to the lifted on-navy tints and the on-navy grey set whenever content sits on an ink band.
Do use environ-ink whenever Environment orange needs to be text on white.
Do state list length in type wherever a list is grouped or filtered.

Do keep motion to the single staggered reveal (opacity + translateY(22px) + blur(6px), .7–.8s on cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.28,1), per-item delay via --d), gate it behind the .js class so content is visible without JS, and neutralise it under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do keep form controls at 1rem or larger and pair the safety-blue focus border with the global 3px crimson focus ring.
Do scope footer-brand typography with descendant selectors (.footer-brand p, .footer-brand .footer-word); a bare class loses to .footer-brand p on specificity.
donts: Don't put a shadow on a content surface — cards, rows, domain blocks, bands. Shadows belong to buttons, the nav drawer and the slide-over only.
Don't introduce a colour that isn't sampled from the logo or a named legibility correction of one.
Don't let a pillar colour become an action, or crimson become a category.
Don't use photography or filled illustration; illustration is authored line-art SVG.
Don't set Overpass Mono on anything that isn't a code, a number or a count.
Don't place the header logo image on the navy footer — its subtitle is black and its emblem navy, neither of which survives; use the typeset .footer-word lockup instead.
Don't change a selected element's footprint; draw selection inset (inset 0 0 0 2px) so list rhythm holds.
Don't exceed the radius vocabulary: 4px for controls and cards, 2px for micro-marks, full circles for small round tokens.
